pr_body:
# Objective

- Fixes #15060

## Solution

- Added `IdentityAssetTransformer<A>` which is an `AssetTransformer` which infallibly returns the input `Asset` unmodified.
- Replaced `LoadAndSave` and `LoadAndSaveSettings` with type definitions linking back to `LoadTransformAndSave` and `LoadTransformAndSaveSettings` respectively.
- Marked `LoadAndSave` and `LoadAndSaveSettings` as depreciated with a migration guide included, hinting to the user to use the underlying type instead.

## Testing

- Ran CI locally

---

## Migration Guide

- Replace `LoadAndSave<L, S>` with `LoadTransformAndSave<L, IdentityAssetTransformer<<L as AssetLoader>::Asset>, S>`
- Replace `LoadAndSaveSettings<L, S>` with `LoadTransformAndSaveSettings<L, (), S>`
pr_comments: I think that adding the `IdentityAssetTransformer` is nice for an easy migration path, and there *are* cases (e.g. file format conversion) where you may want to simply glue together a prewritten loader and a prewritten saver.

issue_context.title: Deprecate `LoadAndSave` asset processor
issue_context.body:
> Technically LoadAndSave also works. All of cart's early asset processors worked in the AssetSaver, instead of a separate transform step. We might want to stop doing that and deprecate LoadAndSave.

_Originally posted by @JMS55 in https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/pull/15058#discussion_r1745895985_
comments: I agree with this: we should have one clear way to do this, and the three-step process is much clearer and more flexible.

review_comments: Bleh, not my favorite. But CompressedImageSaver needs rewriting anyways: https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/issues/14671#issuecomment-2307855809, so it's fine.

Yeah it's definitely ugly. I imagine you'd want to separate out the compression stage from `CompressedImageSaver` into an `AssetTransformer`, but I definitely consider it out of the scope of this work.
This should be linked to in the `LoadTransformAndSave` docs :)
Not sure how I feel about having this considering deprecating this pattern is kind of the reason we're deprecating LoadAndSave in the first place.... but ehh

Agreed! I see `IdentityAssetTransformer` as a necessary evil. As @alice-i-cecile mentioned, file format conversion is a valid use-case for this transformer, and it does massively simplify the migration guide.
